text.p: Following are some of the leading stories in the Swedish papers this morning. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- A crisis in emergency care in the Stockholm region is very serious, according to professor Sten Lindahl, head of the anaesthesia and intensive care unit at the Karolinska hospital. Lindahl has threatened to resign as head of the unit if hospital management insists on seeing through 25-30 percent budget cuts in 1997.
- All households have seen their economy worsen since 1992, particularly families with small children who live in rented flats, according to a report from the postal service's private economy unit.

- One of Sweden's most costly film productions, the Children of the Glassmaker, risks collapse as work has not progressed since this summer. At that time, the budget had been overdrawn by 3.7 million crowns and the project was taken over by film insurance company Ekengrens & Partners.

- Former Swedish Prime Minister Carl Bildt is vague regarding when he will return to Sweden from his current post as EU's High Commissioner, or peacemaker, in Bosnia to ensure that he does not undermine his authority during the time he will remain in Bosnia, according to the paper.
- The Swedish army is treating women worse than the country's air force and navy, according to Eva Lejdbrandt, a female major in the air force.
- A large group of expatriate Chileans is turning against Swedish plans to sell weapons to Chile. About 200 people have signed a letter to the Swedish king, who is on an official visit to Chile.

- An attempt by Sweden's Minister of Interior Jorgen Andersson to halt the privatisation of county-owned housing companies may have unforeseen and severely negative consequences. The government wants to pass a law which will stop the payment of state subsidies to public housing companies which sell more than 25 percent of their holdings.
- Chairman of international engineering company ABB, Swede Percy Barnevik, has become the first non-American to be named to the board of General Motors.

- American investment bank Morgan Stanley's plans to buy 60 percent of real estate company Castellum from state-owned Securum, announced nearly five months ago, has still not been finalised. Castellum holds real estate valued at about eight billion crowns.
- An increase in exports from Sweden to India this year by 50 percent, from 2.1 billion to three billion crowns, has encouraged Swedish banks to set aside money for business opportunities in Inida.
